title: Capacity hedging, autoscale windows, and sovereignty-aware routing for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a coordinated feature set for regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets that reduces failover-induced capacity churn while preserving data residency guarantees. This ticket covers: (1) capacity hedging policies that hold configurable headroom per region to honor throughput guarantees during partial outages, (2) temporal autoscale windows that allow predictable scale-up/down behavior during business-critical time ranges, and (3) sovereignty-aware routing rules that prevent cross-border execution of sensitive requests while providing safe, pre-authorized fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Hedging: Admins can configure a regional headroom percentage (0-30%) and observe reserved capacity metrics in the console.
Autoscale windows: Teams can declare discrete autoscale windows (daily or weekly) with separate min/max and cooldown values; autoscaler honors windows during scale decisions.

Sovereignty routing: Requests tagged with a residency flag are routed to in-region pools; if in-region cannot satisfy SLA, fallback follows a defined policy (deny | enqueue | cross-region with approval).
Failover behavior: During a simulated zone outage, hedging reduces immediate cross-region spill to <10% of requests for committed fleets and preserves throughput guarantees for reserved customers.
Observability: Dashboards show hedged capacity, windowed-scale decisions, and residency routing events with trace IDs linked to requests.
Rollout: Feature gated and canaried to 5% dedicated fleets in us-west-2 for 48 hours with success criteria met before 50% expansion.
tasks: Spec: complete technical design doc and operator runbook (confluence: drive.redwood.com/dedicated/capacity-hedging).
Scheduler: extend lease allocator to support hedged buckets and soft-shrink logic.
Autoscaler: add window aware policy and weighted cooldown calculation to autoscaler service.
Routing: implement sovereignty-aware routing flags and policy engine (deny/enqueue/fallback).
Console: new UI for configuring hedging and autoscale windows; display hedged headroom metrics.
Telemetry: emit hedging events, windowed-scale-decisions, residency-fallback logs and traces.
E2E tests: create integration tests for hedging under node loss and autoscale windows behavior.
Runbook & Support: publish runbook with playbook for partial outages and rollback steps.
Docs: update public docs + API spec to include residency flags and autoscale window API.
Security: schedule KMS review for potential cross-region fallback encryption handling.
decisions: Hedging granularity: hedging will be configured at the regional-pool level (not per-customer) to avoid fragmentation and enable predictable bin-packing.
Soft-shrink: default eviction behavior will be soft-shrink where we mark instances for delayed termination and allow a 5 minute drain to reduce tail latency impact.
Fallback policy: default residency fallback is 'enqueue' (hold request until in-region capacity or until customer-specific approved cross-region fallback is enabled).
Cost tradeoff: default hedging will be conservative (5%) for free-tier and promotional fleets, and configurable up to 25% for SLA-paying customers.
Telemetry retention: hedging and residency events retained for 90 days in analytics for regression analysis.
notes: Motivation: Customer feedback showed cascading cross-region spill during a single-zone GCE maintenance window causing SLA violations and higher egress costs.
Trade-offs: Hedging reduces immediate failover but increases idle GPU hours; autoscale windows reduce thrash but may slow reaction to true traffic spikes.
Compatibility: Works with existing prewarm signals and dedicated capacity contracts; must coordinate with billing team to account for reserved headroom usage.
Open questions: whether hedging should be per-model (heavy models may reserve more) or per-pool only; initial rollout is per-pool with future per-model flag under consideration.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag merge behind org flag. 2) Unit + integration tests pass on CI. 3) Canary to 5% fleets in us-west-2 for 48h; monitor reserved_headroom_utilization, SLA, and cost. 4) Expand to 25% and then to all regions in 2-week increments if no regressions. 5) Post-rollout: 2-week cost/availability review and adjust default hedging thresholds.
testing_plan: Load tests: simulate zone loss with 10k rps to validate <10% cross-region spill for reserved fleets. Chaos: scheduled node-eviction experiments and autoscaler cooling behavior. Security: KMS round-trip when routing fallback to cross-region to verify encryption and key access logging. Cost: run 7-day synthetic workload to estimate additional idle GPU-hours and cost per hedging percent.
last_update: 2026-03-10: Engineering spike completed; scheduler prototype that supports hedged buckets merged to feature branch. Next: autoscaler window policy implementation and console work queued. Open PR: platform#14432. Observability schema proposal under review by SRE.
